derivation: One branch occurrence completed and discharged its obligation while the sibling obligation remained OPEN. The later record shares that occurrence's provider-native operation identity and differs in content, so LIFE-010 classifies it CONFLICTING and LIFE-006 fixes the reason set to CONFLICTING_EFFECT. The disputed occurrence is completed, so LIFE-013's dependency rule runs: the affected set is that occurrence and its transitive descendants, of which it has none, so no active occurrence changes and the open sibling obligation is untouched. The discharged branch obligation's completion frontier is exactly that occurrence, so it becomes DISPUTED while retaining its completion basis. Under LIFE-017 a DISPUTED obligation does not satisfy a join, so the pass can never join in this candidate even after the sibling discharges. The completed row and its selected route remain historical; LIFE-013 does not rewrite earlier permission or completed routing.
